To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dehydration and rehydration processes are important in lubrication of phospholipids, and hyaluric acid can improve lubrication of the phospholipids.
the lubrication properties and the wear resistance of PMPC-granted CLPE are improved by rehydration and hyaluronan.

the start-up friction is reduced and the damage of phospholipids polymer-grafted CLP was suppressed by rehydrating the PMPC layer in water or hyaluornic acid solution, but the start-up friction increased in fetal bovin serum solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influences of dehydration and re-hydration on lubrication properties of polymer-grafted CLP.
the lubrication properties in reciprocating motion of PMPC-granted CLPE in the presence of rehydration and hyaluranic acid.
the lubrication properties in the presence of hyaluronic-acid in various lubricants for the PMPC-graft CLPE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lubrication properties and durability of PMPC-graffed CLPE were enhanced by rehydration and addition of hyaluronic.
the lubrication mechanism of PMPC layer can be switched from the hydration lubrication to boundary lubrication by the rehydration and hyaluronan.
the hydrated phospholipid polymers are effective in reducing wear of the artificial joint material, and the lubrication properties are affected by hydration and the composition of lubricant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lubrication properties can be optimized by the selection of the lubricant for rehydration.

the lubrication mechanism of the PMPC-graft surface is a complex process, which is affected by the hydration state of the PMPC chain, and the lubrication performance is improved by the hydration of the PMPC surface.
hydration lubrication of the PMPC-graft layer is effective for reducing friction in the lubrication condition with rehydration process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydration lubrication of PMPC-grafts can be maintained in the lubrication with rehydration by un-loading and in the lubrication containing hyaluronate.
the lubrication properties can be improved by rehydration in hyaluronic solution.
the lubrication properties are influenced by the lubricant and the hydration state of the polymer layer.
